summary: Weekly POC sync focused on anomaly/regression hunt. Customer reported increased false positives on clinical triage prompts after prompt tuning and a latency spike when KV caching is off. SE walked through recent batch results, discussed tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated footprints for throughput, and agreed on targeted next steps: larger KV-cache-enabled run, security docs, and more edge-case prompts. Agreed to a canary run next week.
topics: recent regression signals in prompt set
canary run plan and success criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Rodriguez: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um quick roll call?
[00:06] Dr. Elena Park: Elena here.
[00:08] Samir Patel: Samir.
[00:10] Juno Morales: Juno.
[00:12] Derek Lim: Derek from Redwood.
[00:15] Maya Rodriguez: Cool ok, agenda — anomaly hunt updates, prompt sandbox results, and next steps. We put the latest bench spreadsheet here: https://redwood.link/pareto-bench-10-13
[00:30] Samir Patel: Quick context, since last week we pushed the revised triage prompt set into the prod-like env and saw an uptick in false positives, meaning the model flags more items as high-priority when they should be low. Also latency spiked for longer histories when KV cache was disabled in that test.
[00:50] Derek Lim: Right yeah we saw that in the 1k sample. The prefix cache gave about 28% lower p99 when it's warmed. When it's cold and no KV, p50 looks okay but p95/p99 jumps.
[01:10] Dr. Elena Park: Can you remind me which model variant you ran? Was that the 8-bit quant or the float16? I'm getting the names mixed from the sheet.
[01:22] Derek Lim: We ran three profiles — baseline fp16, q4_0, and q5_k. The naming in the sheet is a little terse, apologies. It was q5_k that lost some fidelity on multi-step clinical prompts. Might be the tokenization edge.
[01:40] Samir Patel: That's the issue, the outputs started hallucinating small meds names, e.g., "amoxin" instead of "amoxicillin" a couple times. Not catastrophic but we need tighter guardrails.
[01:55] Maya Rodriguez: Okay noted. Two parallel threads then: one is fidelity/guardrail tightening, the other is infra — cache, batch sizing, dedicated pool?
[02:10] Juno Morales: From compliance side we also want full audit fields for every decision: model_version, quant_profile, KV_cache_hit boolean, request_id, user_id obfuscated, and retention window. Is that supported?
[02:26] Derek Lim: Yes, we can emit all those fields. We log them to the private control plane. For Private/VPC deployments, logs can be forwarded to customer's SIEM and they control retention. Slight caveat: for Hosted API there are standard retention defaults but we can map them in the contract.
[02:46] Maya Rodriguez: Great. We put together a trimmed security pack, I'll share SOC2 excerpts and the KMS integration notes after the call.
[02:55] Samir Patel: Thanks. Back to the fuzz — can we see examples where cache-warmed vs cold changed the decision?
[03:05] Derek Lim: Yeah I pulled two examples into the bench sheet, rows 112 and 233, they show the prefix tokens in play and the KV cache hit status. In one case the second-turn prompt lost context because the kvcache pointer shifted, we think it's token overflow with q4_0.
[03:30] Dr. Elena Park: When you say token overflow do you mean sequence length trimming? We're on a 2k window in infra but actual messages sometimes hit 2.6k after appended metadata.
[03:44] Derek Lim: Exactly, trimming happens and then the model sees less context. We can recommend either moving to a dedicated pool with longer sequence optimized kernels or enforce client-side trimming and prefix summarization. Both are viable.
[04:00] Maya Rodriguez: For the customer success metrics — what's our success criteria for the canary? Elena?
[04:06] Dr. Elena Park: Reduce false positive rate by 60% on the labelled set, keep p95 latency under 900ms for triage calls, and no severity-level hallucinations in the 200-case audit.
[04:20] Maya Rodriguez: Good clear numbers. Derek, can you run a 2k-case batch with cache enabled and the q5_k profile and compare to fp16? Also include token counts per request and cost delta.
[04:33] Derek Lim: Yep, I'll run q5_k w/ KV on, q4_0 w/ KV on, and fp16 as baseline. I'll include costing using our unit-cost model. Expect a matrix by next Tuesday.
[04:45] Samir Patel: On the guardrail tightening — can Redwood support turning on a lightweight reranker or a confidence threshold layer? We saw that a simple calibrated filter reduced noise in prior pilots.
[04:56] Derek Lim: We have a built-in reranker option in the pipeline that runs a small embed-based re-score, it's low-latency if you avoid batching it across many requests. There's also an ensemble threshold approach; we can prototype it in the sandbox.
[05:12] Juno Morales: Would that extra reranker create more PII in logs? We want to ensure any intermediate representation isn't stored.
[05:20] Derek Lim: Good point — by default reranker runs ephemeral and only stores final decision metadata. We can disable storing intermediate embeddings and show the audit trace that only includes final scores.
[05:30] Maya Rodriguez: We're seeing common themes: quantization-induced fidelity loss, sequence trimming causing context loss, and missed guardrail threshold. Plan is: Derek runs the batch, Maya shares security pack, Pareto uploads more edge prompts. Then we do a canary.
[05:45] Samir Patel: Timeline looks tight but doable. One more question — if the canary fails, what rollback plan do we have?
[05:51] Derek Lim: Canary will run against shadow traffic first and we have automatic rollback to the pinned model version. On Dedicated, rollback is faster and we can pin to previous commit. For Hosted, we have a fallback route to a safer fp16 variant with slightly higher cost but stable outputs.
[06:10] Dr. Elena Park: Are there privacy concerns with the shadow traffic? We can't route real PHI outside the VPC.
[06:18] Maya Rodriguez: For customers with PHI we recommend Private/VPC deployment or a dedicated tenant; otherwise we use synthetic or de-identified traffic for canary. We'll adhere to your compliance constraints.
[06:32] Samir Patel: Ok noted. About cost — can you estimate unit cost difference between fp16 and q5_k for our workload? Ballpark is fine.
[06:40] Derek Lim: Ballpark — fp16 is about 1.0x token-cost baseline, q5_k tends to be 0.6x token-cost but may require more steps/temperature tuning which can increase tokens per request. Net savings typically 10–30% for many triage workloads but we need the matrix to be precise.
[06:58] Maya Rodriguez: I'll note that in the next steps.
[07:02] [08:00] (snippets omitted: Derek narrates detailed sample diffs from bench sheet)
[08:10] Samir Patel: We also discovered a user-flow where appended metadata duplicates — that inflated token count and led to both cost and latency spikes. We need a client-side dedupe step.
[08:25] Derek Lim: Yep simple preprocessor dedupe reduces tokens by ~15% in our tests. We'll include a suggested preproc snippet in the repo.
[08:40] Dr. Elena Park: Quick ask from compliance — can you surface cryptographic proof of key rotation for KMS and the HSM attestation?
[08:49] Maya Rodriguez: We'll include the KMS integration notes and the HSM attestation excerpt in the security pack.
[09:00] Samir Patel: Any blockers from Redwood's side to run the larger KV-enabled batch?
[09:06] Derek Lim: No blockers, just need the labelled examples and we'll queue it on our infra. If you want Dedicated pool we can schedule it but it takes lead time.
[09:18] Marco Li: If we go Dedicated, what's the commit level? We're still evaluating usage.
[09:24] Maya Rodriguez: For Dedicated we do reserved capacity contracts monthly/annual. You can start with a burst-enabled pilot which reduces lead time and you can convert to reserved later. We'll send the pricing tiers.
[09:36] Samir Patel: Ok let's do the KV run first. If that fixes fidelity without Dedicated, we probably stay Hosted.
[09:42] Dr. Elena Park: Agree. Also Derek, can you add a check in the bench sheet to flag token-trim events automatically?
[09:49] Derek Lim: Yes I can add a 'trim_flag' column and auto-detect when sequence length exceeded window and what was trimmed.
[09:58] Maya Rodriguez: Perfect. Last thing — recap and who does what?
[10:03] Maya Rodriguez: Derek runs batch and posts matrix (due 2026-10-20). Maya shares security pack and benchmark link (due 2026-10-15). Elena uploads 100 edge cases (due 2026-10-16). Juno sends audit fields list (due 2026-10-18).
[10:18] Samir Patel: I'll review the matrix and schedule the canary.
[10:22] Dr. Elena Park: Thanks everyone.
[10:25] Derek Lim: Thanks, we'll follow up in thread with results and a short video walk-through.
[10:30] Maya Rodriguez: Meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription may have small mis-hearings (model variant names). Shared artifacts: bench spreadsheet (https://redwood.link/pareto-bench-10-13), security pack (to be sent), preproc snippet (repo: https://git.redwood/pareto-sandbox).
